newsitem.title: FINLAND: Cultor says Japan okays xylitol in food.
newsitem.headline: Cultor says Japan okays xylitol in food.

text.p: Finnish food ingredients, feeds and bakery group Cultor Oy said in a statement on Monday that Japan's ministry of health and welfare had approved xylitol as a food additive.

"Japan is the last significant market to be opened up," Cultor said, adding that its Xyrofin division was the world's leading producer of xylitol -- a five-carbon sugar alcohol used in a variety of confectionery applications like chewing gum, and in oral care products and pharmaceuticals.
Cultor saw good prospects in Japan for xylitol.
"Xylitol is expected to make a large impact in invigorating the sugar-free market in Japan and is already generating considerable commercial and scientific interest," it said.

"Japan is considered to be one of the most promising markets for new xylitol product launches, and a market which will contribute significant growth to the xylitol business in coming years," Cultor said.
Due to continuing growth in xylitol markets gobally and anticipating the Japanese approval, Xyrofin had invested in the past two years in increased xylitol production capacity, it said.
